subject: Audit streaming window + SSO token rotation — ops plan and exceptions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit streaming window + SSO token rotation — initial ask

Team —

I had a follow-up call with Acme SecOps this morning and they raised two operational asks that we need to triage:

1) Audit streaming window: they want an "append-only" audit feed that includes full event context for 90 days for Dedicated accounts, with the option to set shorter retention (30/7 days) per contract. They cited regulators who require 90 days of tamper-evident logs.

2) SSO token rotation: Acme asked for a documented token rotation SLA for SCIM/SSO connectors and an emergency rekey process. They want a clear ops playbook if a token is compromised.

Attached is a quick sketch (audit_window_proposal_v1.pdf) and an initial rotation matrix (sso_token_rotation_matrix.xlsx).

Questions I want us to resolve in this thread:
- Feasibility: can runtime support a configurable audit window per dedicated customer without blowing up GPU/ingress costs?
- Security implications: how does BYOK/KMS impact our ability to provide a tamper-evident stream (if keys are customer-managed)?
- Roadmap: can Product/Infra prioritize a small-scope implementation (90/30/7 presets) as an Enterprise toggle for Q4?

Next steps I propose: Karthik to estimate infra work, Mina to map security controls and exception language, Marissa to slot a small RFC for the roadmap. Connor — please note any customer-facing docs we need to update.

Thanks,

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit streaming window + SSO token rotation — initial ask

Ben / team —

Thanks, Ben. Quick notes from infra perspective after skimming the attachments:

- Audit window: we can produce an event stream (Kafka/SQS) from the control plane at the requested fidelity. Cost & complexity come from two things: (a) retaining event payloads in storage for 90 days (S3 lifecycle + immutability layer) and (b) per-customer encryption keys for archived blobs. For Dedicated customers we can enable a "long-retention bucket" option that is isolated, but we should limit realtime streaming retention (hot storage) to 7 days to keep replay latency low.

- BYOK/KMS: if customer supplies keys (BYOK), we can still write an append-only hash chain but we must ensure signing is done with a Redwood-managed signing key (separate from encryption) to guarantee server-side tamper evidence. If the customer holds the only signing material, that breaks our ability to vouch for immutability on our side.

- Implementation estimate (ballpark): 6–8 engineer-weeks to deliver the isolation + retention lifecycle + streaming hooks (small team: infra + storage). 2–3 additional weeks for integration tests and documentation.

I'll follow up with a short RFC skeleton by EOD Wednesday. For prioritization, this seems Enterprise-critical and should be a candidate for Q4 backlog if Sales confirms multiple Commit customers.

—Karthik

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit streaming window + SSO token rotation — initial ask

Team —

Security checklist and exceptions notes: please consider these items when drafting requirements.

- Tamper evidence: as Karthik noted, signing must be Redwood-controlled to attest immutability. If a customer requests BYOK for encryption, we should still maintain a separate signing key in HSM (or KMS with signing capability) under Redwood control. Add this as a contractual requirement for "Redwood-attested audit streams."

- Data residency: some customers (Acme included) require regional storage. We need the option to create the long-retention bucket in their selected region to meet compliance. This adds deployment complexity but is doable.

- Token rotation SLA: recommend a documented 24-hour RTO for revocation + re-provisioning with an emergency manual flow and a 7-day rotation cadence for automated tokens. Acceptable exceptions: customers that cannot support SCIM re-provisioning for 3rd-party IdPs — in those cases we should require an incident playbook and network-level compensating controls.

- Evidence packaging: we should be able to export a tamper-evident ZIP (signed manifest + logs) on request for audits. That should be an ops feature request tied to this work.

I'll draft proposed contract language for "Redwood-attested audit streams" and a short SSO rotation SLA clause.

—Mina
Security & Compliance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acme.com>, okta-sec@okta.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit streaming window + SSO token rotation — initial ask

Thanks for the estimates and security notes. Copying ACME so they see the proposed approach.

Plan / owners:
- Karthik: RFC + infra estimate (deliverable: RFC doc + cost model) — due 2026-09-08
- Mina: Contract language + SSO rotation SLA draft (deliverable: contract clause + playbook sketch) — due 2026-09-01
- Ben: Confirm which Dedicated customers need the 90-day default and capture any procurement constraints from Acme — due 2026-08-28
- Connor: Update public-facing docs/FAQ and create a short customer-facing FAQ page for Sales — due 2026-09-10

One operational exception to call out: until we have the long-retention bucket fully isolated, we can offer a short-term mitigation to Acme — daily exports of their audit events into a customer-controlled S3 (signed manifest). That's somewhat manual but buys time for a full implementation.

Acme / Alice — would that temporary export be acceptable as an interim remediation? If yes, Ben please propose a cadence and storage location.

I'll schedule a 30-minute triage next week to align scope if folks are available.

Marissa
Group PM, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
